mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP signals strong economic growth, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances following a 3-month GDP increase, or if the correlation between GDP growth and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production index by more than 1% within a month signals a slowdown in economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in real GDP and housing starts by more than 1% each within a quarter signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer and business confidence rise.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the joint correlation between GDP and housing starts increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 jobs within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate profits.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the consumer price index by more than 0.5% within a month signals inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate monetary tightening.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 70% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real final sales of goods by more than 1% within a month signals a contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings are expected to decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS decreases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
